years_since_diagnosis.evidence: Crohn's for about six years now

location.evidence: Colonoscopy revealed Crohn's throughout colon, some small intestine involvement.

severity.evidence: Symptoms persist year-round, need bathroom every hour, business suffering significantly, required escalation to biologic after multiple prior treatments failed or were contraindicated.

disease_control.evidence: Currently on Entyvio three months in — 'too early to tell if working'; budesonide 'helps somewhat but not long-term solution'; still needing bathroom every hour and losing business accounts.

treatments.reason_stopped: Kidney function started declining; nephrologist said stop immediately.
treatments.evidence: Started conservatively with mesalamine. Helped initially. Then kidney function started declining. Nephrologist said stop immediately.
Tried dietary management. Some improvement but not enough.
Started budesonide. Fewer systemic effects, easier on kidneys. Helps somewhat but not long-term solution.
Finally approved. Started three months ago. Too early to tell if working.

encounters.evidence: Finally saw doctor. Colonoscopy revealed Crohn's throughout colon...
GI wants biologics... Finally convinced doctors to try Entyvio.
Nephrologist said stop immediately... nephrologist concerned. Immune suppression with kidney disease risky.

status.evidence: Finally approved. Started three months ago.

barriers.evidence: Nephrologist concerned. Immune suppression with kidney disease risky. Caught between two specialists disagreeing.
Insurance denied three times. Said not proven safe with kidney disease. Four months of appeals. Finally approved.

referral_steps_gp_to_prescriber.evidence: GP -> GI specialist (who prescribed Entyvio). Nephrologist was a side consult, not a referral step toward the biologic prescriber.

extraction_notes: Dietary management included as a treatment given it was explicitly tried as a Crohn's management strategy after mesalamine was stopped. Nephrologist encounter marked on_referral_path=false as it was a parallel specialist consultation, not a step in the referral chain to the biologic prescriber. Disease control marked 'partial' rather than 'poor' because budesonide provides some relief and Entyvio outcome is still unknown at 3 months. Comorbidities: chronic kidney disease only; NSAIDs mentioned as cause but are not a Crohn's treatment. Fatigue inferred from 'infusions exhausting', 'whole day lost', 'working myself into grave'; urgency inferred from 'need bathroom every hour'.
